resource.name: Education NYC
resource.description: This dataset presents the 2009–2010 CPS Progress Report results for all schools as of February 2, 2011. Schools are compared only within the same level (Elementary, K-8, Middle, High, Transfer), and peer indexes are calculated differently by level. For Elementary and K-8 schools, the peer index ranges from 0 to 100 and is based on demographic factors such as % ELL, % Special Education, % Title I free lunch, and % Black/Hispanic, with higher values indicating greater student need. For Middle and High Schools, the peer index ranges from 1.00 to 4.50 and incorporates prior proficiency measures and student characteristics, with lower values indicating greater student need.
columns_description: Grade assigned each school based on school environment, student performance & student progress any additional recongnition obtained on exemplary student outcomes. Scores are based on comparing results from one school to peer schools.
Peer indexes are calculated differently depends on school level.  Schools are compared to other schools in same school level (ex. Elementary, K-8, Middle, High School, High school transfer)
Environment score reflect measuring pre-conditions for learning, student attendance and other aspects, such as high expectations, engagement, safety, respect and communication in school.
Average student attendance rate for the school year 2009-2010. Higher attendance rates may correlate with better school performance and grades.
Ratio of teachers to students in the school. A lower ratio often indicates more personalized attention for students, potentially leading to better outcomes.
Percentage of students who are English Language Learners (ELL) in the school. This demographic factor can influence the resources and strategies needed for effective teaching.
Percentage of students receiving special education services. This can impact the school's resource allocation and overall performance.
A score reflecting the safety of the school environment, including incidents of violence or bullying. Safer schools often have better learning environments.
A score indicating the level of parent engagement and involvement in school activities. Higher engagement can lead to better student outcomes.
Rate of student participation in extracurricular activities. Engagement in such activities can enhance student development and school performance.
Average years of teaching experience among the school's faculty. More experienced teachers may contribute to better student outcomes.
A score assessing the quality and condition of the school's physical facilities. Better facilities can enhance the learning environment.
Percentage of students eligible for Title I funding, indicating economic disadvantage. This can affect the resources available to the school.
